name: BHFS pattern (rodent LI-rTMS timing) at Oz
origin: Rodger lab (UWA, Perth) and Sherrard lab (Sorbonne); pattern from Global Energy Medicine patent PCT/AU2007/000454
summary: Copies the timing of "biomimetic high-frequency stimulation" (BHFS, Grehl et al. 2016) from rodent low-intensity rTMS studies: 62.6-ms trains of 20 pulses repeated at 6.55 Hz for 1 min, 9.75 Hz for 8 min and 6.15 Hz for 1 min, on one coil at Oz. The rodent fields were about 1000-4000 times stronger.
notes: Grehl et al. 2016 define BHFS (pattern from patent PCT/AU2007/000454, Global Energy Medicine) as 300-us monophasic pulses, 108,840 per 10-min session, at about 10 mT on target with rise times under 100 us. Dufor et al. 2019 (8-10 mT) and Seewoo et al. 2018 (about 13 mT at cortex) report effects in rodents, while Dufor found 4.5 mT ineffective; Moretti & Rodger 2022 give 1-150 mT for rodent LI-rTMS. All evidence is from rodents and cultures. Dufor 2019 claim a cryptochrome-dependent mechanism (single lab), and Grehl model the induced field at only about 0.05 V/m at 10 mT. This program gives at most 5 uT at 20 mm and copies the timing only; nothing is known about humans at uT, and it is not a treatment. Grehl et al. do not give the spacing of the 20 pulses inside a train; the table spaces them evenly at 3.13 ms (62.6 ms / 20), slightly closer than the about 3.3 ms implied if the last pulse ends at 62.6 ms. Each 300-us pulse becomes one 0.5-ms tick at full scale, and every pulse onset lands within about 0.5 ms of its exact time on the 2-kHz grid; the fast rise of the original cannot be reproduced. The evidence rating refers to the rodent and culture studies, not to this pattern at uT. No human placement exists: the single coil at Oz is an arbitrary probe after the mouse visual-cortex work of Makowiecki et al. 2014, which used a related BHFS-like pattern (59.9-ms trains at 6.67/10.01/6.25 Hz, about 8 mT). There is no fade-in or fade-out, so the three stages keep their exact lengths and pulse counts (393, 4680 and 369 trains). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if you feel unwell.
setting: No human setting is published; all data are from rodents and cell cultures.
schedule: Rodent protocols ran 10 min a day for 14 days (Dufor 2019) or once a week for 4 weeks (Seewoo 2018). No human schedule has been tested.
source: Grehl et al. 2016, Front Neural Circuits (BHFS definition and device) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5093126/ ; Dufor et al. 2019, Sci Adv https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821463/ ; Moretti & Rodger 2022 (LI-rTMS review) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9846462/ ; Seewoo et al. 2018, Sci Rep (coil and field) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5928106/ ; Makowiecki et al. 2014, J Neurosci (BHFS-like pattern over mouse visual cortex) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25100609/ ; Global Energy Medicine, patent PCT/AU2007/000454 (cited by Grehl 2016)
